# Signatories and community support

Shaurita D. Hutchins and Samuel Bharti are PhD candidates at the University of Alabama at Birmingham and will co-lead the project.

**Hutchins will lead educational design and community development.** She will coordinate the example tutorials and develop the metadata schema. She will draw on her experience in open-source training and Carpentries instruction to write accessibility guidance and establish the contribution process. Trained in genetics, genomics, and bioinformatics, she combines computational biology with reproducible R/Bioconductor workflows. Her [Prioritizing Candidate Genetic Variants Using GTEx, HuBMAP, and IDG](https://cfdetrainingcenter.github.io/candidate-genetic-variants/) module for the CFDE Training Center includes coding activities that run in the browser and knowledge checks.

**Bharti will lead software architecture and engine integration.** He will build adapters that use existing engine checks and produce validation reports in a common format. His teaching work includes [r-for-beginners](https://github.com/samuelbharti/r-for-beginners), an adaptation of Software Carpentry lessons with slides. He also develops the R packages bioclients, biohttp, and biobouncer, and publishes package documentation through GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages.

We will jointly design the package API and registry, and share responsibility for governance and the example tutorials.

We requested public feedback through [r/Stats](https://www.reddit.com/r/Stats/comments/1wvj3wd/for_people_who_teach_or_learn_r_how_do_you_find/) and the [learnr webR discussion](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/issues/766#issuecomment-5944771998). Community contributor [\@coatless](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/issues/766#issuecomment-5944898742) pointed us to learnr2 and Quarto Live. That feedback helped us focus on shared metadata and checks, though the proposed schema still needs review. We will seek engine maintainers' feedback on the schema and the checks each adapter can support.

We will also consult Carpentries and Bioconductor educators, along with university and community instructors. We will add documented feedback and letters of support as received.
